bundles.instructions: Base objects; Bob and reader ServiceAccount have no resource grant yet. Bootstrap/install is done by fixture owner, never by Alice/Bob.
Start from core. This RoleBinding grants Bob only demo-dev pod reads.
Reset before use. Not cumulative with the previous variant; grants pod reads, not node or secret access.
Reset before use. Named get of a cluster-scoped object only.
Add only to this scenario; reader does not already include these rights.
Issuer fixture gives Bob raw groups readers and log-readers. Mapping produces team:readers and team:log-readers; bindings still supply the permissions.
Install only for admission scenario. Core mutating phase is a no-op. Submit each ConfigMap as a separate request; the rejected proposal must never be persisted.
First object should pass, second should fail policy; these are requests, not preloaded storage state.

Worker builds the local demo reader image and pins its digest for any live run. The example is deliberately not a downloadable third-party workload. Explicit projection still works with automatic mounting disabled. For API TLS, provide trusted CA separately; never skip server verification.
This is the success grant; omit it for the authenticated-but-forbidden branch.
Reset before use. Grants reader within demo-dev to its ServiceAccounts only.
Reset before use. The global subject group expands who may read demo-dev, but this RoleBinding still limits granted resource scope to demo-dev.
Dedicated reviewer credential; never confuse this with the token submitted for review.

Substitute observed UID and exact issued token; templates are not ready-to-send credentials. TokenRequest POST /api/v1/namespaces/demo-dev/serviceaccounts/reader/token; TokenReview POST /apis/authentication.k8s.io/v1/tokenreviews. Authorization header on review uses the reviewer credential, not spec.token.
Operator is separately authenticated. Bob has direct reader permission; group impersonation is not assumed. Header Impersonate-User: oidc:bob.
ConstrainedImpersonation enabled. Reset/remove all legacy impersonate grants before this variant. Omit either identity or action grant for a negative branch; no node scope.
Editor possesses pod-read and RBAC object create/get only. Role create and binding create still face anti-escalation checks.
Submitting this as oidc:editor must fail. It is not preinstalled.
Fixture owner creates this role before testing a forbidden binding. Role existence alone gives editor no secret access.
Submit as oidc:editor against the owner-seeded role. Editor can create RoleBindings but cannot bind this role; no binding may persist.
A different principal oidc:binding-editor has no reader rights. It receives only RoleBinding create and bind of reader, demonstrating both necessary permissions.

fixture.configCaveat: API server adds system:authenticated after external mapping; validation example constrains mapped issuer groups. Worker must validate exact v1 schema and evaluation order against selected tag before presenting runnable YAML. No --oidc-* arguments may be combined with --authentication-config.

globalRequirements: Create a dedicated Kubernetes navigation/workspace group with Human access, Token validation, Authorization/RBAC, Workload identity, and Delegation/extensions families. JWT foundations are their own shared family linked from K8s and existing OAuth/OIDC/JWE lessons. Do not bury Kubernetes inside generic OAuth or silently duplicate existing lessons.

Use canonical events, explicit actor-local holdings and immutable artifact/generation IDs. Track received bytes, parsed untrusted claims, verified signature, validated claims, mapped userInfo, authorization input/verdict, admission proposal/verdict, persisted object and response separately. Reading a claim never creates permission.

Model API authentication/RBAC/admission as local API-server stages; different swimlanes may explain responsibilities but must not fabricate network hops. The API server may read from watch caches; a symbolic storage boundary must not imply every read makes a new etcd network RPC.

Each scenario has a fixed happy path and independently selectable failures with declared policy. Branches must alter the relevant request/claim/key/rule/state, not only the narration. Do not silently recover into another authenticator or grant.

JWT validation requires primary-source rules and profile-specific requirements. Public key retrieval is not proof of trust by itself. Never expose issuer private keys, refresh tokens or plaintext JWE contents to actors that do not possess them. Bearer token display is synthetic and clearly labeled.

Maintain overview/field/exact-object replay parity. Exact history must retain token envelope versus decrypted/validated representation, principal origin, binding rule and namespace; backwards seek must rebuild state deterministically and clear stale grants/results.

Provide a visible decision strip: credential → identity → requested action → matching grant → admission when relevant → result. Show why a step is skipped. Error cards name failing stage, caller identity, actual status and next meaningful action; do not map all 403s to RBAC.

Navigation, source/profile expanders and scenario switches need keyboard focus return, readable 390px layout, no token overflow, accessible branch labels and no color-only success signal. Keep five or fewer actors horizontally; break browser/login and API authorization into linked phases without losing artifacts.

Source panel pins release/profile/feature maturity, RFC section or Kubernetes section, retrieval date, implementation-specific cache policy and limits. Mark symbolic fixtures as symbolic; cryptographic validity requires separately computed test vectors rather than decorative signatures.

Tests should prove state boundaries and failure behavior, not mirror prose. Test route registration, all declared scenario IDs, preservation of existing OIDC/JWT/JWE paths, policy reset, identity mapping, exact-request RBAC decisions, JWT/key/token rotation, representation custody, no post-rejection persistence, and actual mounted field-to-exact-history transitions.

Before claiming runnable Kubernetes conformance, validate config/manifests and critical status/feature behavior against pinned v1.37.1 executable or source. Native-browser evidence remains separate from DOM tests and from live Kubernetes interoperability. Report any source discrepancy instead of inventing a consensus.

windowsSharedContracts.scope: 14 core scenarios WLOG01-08 and WELEV01-06; optional WELEV07. Existing ADDS crypto, SMB3.1.1, RDP and WinRM lessons are reused/cross-linked, not rewritten.
profiles: Windows11 supported Enterprise/Pro workstation reference with exact build/servicing date recorded before product-specific claims; ADDS Server2025 target where applicable. No implicit Entra join, Microsoft account, consumer Hello or automatic sign-in.
Classic UAC examples explicitly select legacy/classic Admin Approval Mode and a non-built-in administrator. Administrator protection is a separate current feature with an evidence gate.

Credential Guard state must be recorded: keep opaque LSA credential handles by default; if enabled, represent LSAIso/VBS custody without claiming every secret is plaintext in LSASS. Cached-verifier, local-SAM and service-ticket limits remain distinct.
modelRules: Use local-call/local-check/local-create events for Winlogon, LSA, SAM, token and AppInfo operations. Do not turn local OS API calls into network packets or describe every such operation as RFC protocol traffic.
Separate credential collection, validation, local logon eligibility, token creation, process creation, profile/desktop readiness, resource access and the user learning a result.

Every token has owner/logon-context/primary-or-impersonation type, user SID, attributed group SIDs, privileges plus enabled flags, integrity/elevation metadata and lifecycle; token copies are not independent authenticated users.
Keep raw input, account verifier, cached verifier, certificate/private-key handle, Kerberos credential and token as different artifacts. Permission to inspect is not possession.
Group/PAC information is attributable to its authority; local policy/alias additions are separate. Do not imply every unlock/elevation refreshes all existing tokens.
Author source/protection/decoded-acceptance events and cleanup/release histories for every readable result. Never give an observer future server/DC knowledge at request or wire receipt.
Diagram logical LSA/authentication-package/SAM/token roles within the same workstation with parent grouping. Keep no more than five horizontal actors; group or split a detailed stage.
ux: At all times show: device membership, console account authority, local process SID/account, outbound identity, effective logon/elevation policy, and current authentication-versus-authorization decision.

Offer explicit local/domain and classic/Administrator-protection profile selectors before playback, with a textual explanation of what changes. Profile choice resets history rather than mutating a running principal.

Provide token comparison tables and simple labels: credential verified, console allowed, token created, desktop ready, resource allowed. Separate consent, credential verification, local PIN entry and network authentication.
Cross-link exact accepted SMB/AD scenario IDs and retain return-to-origin context; avoid duplicating catalog entries that merely restate an existing protocol flow.
gates: Before code, capture relevant official page/spec bytes, final URL, revision/build scope, retrieval date and SHA256 under the listed snapshotReference paths; sourceSnapshotStatus must remain pending until bytes exist.

Pin MS-KILE/MS-PAC current versions and revalidate the existing AD03/AD04 Windows profile gates. Do not copy older weak mapping, SHA1/RSA-transport or universal fallback claims from broad legacy articles.

Resolve current Administrator-protection support-label discrepancy. Offline smart-card and WHfB detailed flows are named research branches, not silently omitted promises or fabricated implementations.

For declared product support, record Windows edition/build, DC build, effective policies, token inspection and narrowly scoped logs/traces. Synthetic tests establish authored-model consistency, not interoperability.
verification: Tests must assert actual negative boundaries and identity/held-object states, not only that scenario labels/step counts exist. Cover wrong-password /netonly launch, cached/no-cache split, same-name SID separation, DC-required unlock, consent-vs-credentials, UAC cancellation, and all key custody transitions reused from AD.

Add field/held-object replay for token creation/consumption/release and protected-result acceptance. For WIN-11 cleanup, author H-local acceptor-subkey creation in six fixed/seven derived raw-CredSSP/RDP profiles without adding the secret to wire objects. Keep its P3 scope separate and do not reopen accepted WIN01-10.

Native UI checks: keyboard through profile selection/prompt/result, readable token comparison at narrow width, no hidden outcome after denial, and correct return cross-links. Root retains existing broader manual/accessibility gates.

humanRequirements.heading: NFS access: implementation plan
humanRequirements.text: Build NFS01-NFS13. NFS01 is the modern NFSv4.2 entry point. NFS14 is an optional , separately gated advanced followup. Use one shared fixture engine with named inputs, not every version×security×platform permutation. These IDs replace the earlier provisional NFS-01…NFS-12 backlog numbering; match by lesson title, not numeric position. Old AUTH_SYS-v4.0 and Kerberos-v4.0 entries are consolidated in NFS05; explicit nonjoined-client and connection-binding lessons are added.

humanRequirements.heading: Version and platform rules
humanRequirements.text: NFSv3 Separate MOUNTv3 path; AUTH_SYS and RPCSEC_GSS comparison. RFC1813 is Informational; RFC2623 supplies the Kerberos integration. Do not import historical DES examples.

humanRequirements.heading: Version and platform rules
humanRequirements.text: NFSv4.0 Integrated namespace and state; version-specific SETCLIENTID path. Required implementation support includes Kerberos krb5/krb5i/krb5p, but does not require selecting it for every mount.

humanRequirements.heading: Version and platform rules
humanRequirements.text: NFSv4.1 Sessions, slots and optional state protection. RFC8881: client krb5/krb5i MUST, client krb5p SHOULD; server krb5/krb5i/krb5p MUST. Distinguish required support from configured selection.

humanRequirements.heading: Version and platform rules
humanRequirements.text: NFSv4.2 - default Use published RFC7862 with RFC8178; retain the v4.1 base machinery. NFSv4 minor version 2 does not itself turn on TLS, user authentication or optional v4.2 features.

humanRequirements.heading: Version and platform rules
humanRequirements.text: Windows comparison Linux client → Windows Server2025 NFSv4.1. Built-in Windows Client: v2/v3. Windows Server: v2/v3/v4.1 per current Microsoft table. No v4.2 or built-in v4.1 client claim.

humanRequirements.heading: Version and platform rules
humanRequirements.text: The checked replacement work is rfc8881bis-11, 23 September2026 , still an Internet-Draft. It does not replace published RFC8881 requirements. The contemporary TLS1.3 publication is RFC9846 (July2026), which obsoletes RFC8446. Recheck source status at implementation freeze; do not upgrade standards solely from draft wording.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Profile metadata must name NFS major/minor version, RPCSEC_GSS version, selected sec service, mechanism/QOP/enctype, xprtsec, transport, state-protection policy, mapping adapter, authorization policy, source revisions and support evidence. A standards-based illustration is not a live interoperability badge.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: The Linux model is pinned to the retrieved upstream manual snapshot and official kernel documentation, not an invented running build. Before any native-support badge, record actual kernel/config, nfs-utils, Kerberos library, optional gssproxy/tlshd/ktls-utils versions and one verified combination. Do not block offline core modeling on privileged native mounts.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Use stable objects for user/machine TGT and service ticket, local credential cache, service-key handle, GSS initiator/acceptor context and generation, sequence window, clientid, sessionid, slot request/cache, connection association, filehandle/stateid, identity map, export/file policy, TLS certificates/keys and exact packet instances. A handle is not a transferable bearer authorization.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Each network operation has send → receiver wire receipt → local decode/verification → accepted protocol effect. Sender knowledge of success waits for accepted response. Integrity-only content can be visible before verification but is not accepted; encrypted content cannot appear early. Check this in canonical holdings and every field/object replay.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Compute deterministic structural state: identities, operation order, XDR fields, service/tuple choices, sequence-window and slot decisions, exact references, policy outcomes and lifetimes. All crypto output remains SYM unless separately implemented against published numeric vectors. Label symbolic derivations as such; they are not proof of byte-level conformance.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Render protocol-defined local derivations and real decrypt/verify/use actions as replayable operations. Preserve genuine inspect-only context. Do not regress NET-05 by attaching encrypted packet fields only as glossary inspection entries.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Client initiator, server acceptor and KDC retain separate key custody. Server service keys and TLS private keys stay with their owners; GSS context handles never imply export of keys. Document the selected Kerberos context-key/subkey relation rather than simply copying a single session-key label everywhere.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Authentication outcome, effective authorization identity, export decision, file permission, operation result, and client acceptance are separate state paths. No server-generated response grants client knowledge before its verification event. Negative inputs stop at their first actual detector and retain unrelated accepted state.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: For each added native operation/error, author an independent protocol worksheet with source section, legal operation placement, relevant status and detector before fixtures. Do not derive expected test outcomes from the scenario under test.

humanRequirements.heading: Source caveats and bounded followups
humanRequirements.text: RPC9289 section5 says server ALPN appears in ServerHello, while current TLS1.3/IANA place ALPN in EncryptedExtensions. Model TLS1.3 correctly: ClientHello offer and encrypted server EncryptedExtensions selection sunrpc. Record this source discrepancy; do not call it a verified erratum. The RFC Editor errata endpoint was inaccessible on2026-10-21. The worker must recheck it and record the actual disposition at source freeze; absence of an errata result is not proof none exists.

humanRequirements.heading: Source caveats and bounded followups
humanRequirements.text: RFC9266 section4.1 restricts reuse of tls-exporter binding across authentication mechanism instances. NFS14 deliberately uses one user/context and closes its teaching connection. A multiuser combined GSS/TLS implementation needs a separately sourced binding design; do not infer it from ordinary Linux mount options.

humanRequirements.heading: Source caveats and bounded followups
humanRequirements.text: The official kernel GSS page says RPCSEC_GSSv3 is not implemented. Keep Full Mode Labeled NFS, multi-principal/subject-label assertions and advanced GSSv3 delegation as standards-only research until a named implementation proves support.

humanRequirements.heading: Source caveats and bounded followups
humanRequirements.text: Retain Labeled NFS, inter-server COPY/delegation and pNFS data-server authorization as bounded later work, not fourteen more permutations. Each requires its own selected feature/layout/mode, source worksheet, extra actors and implementation evidence. Limited Server label storage is not Full Mode MAC enforcement; a layout is not universal user authorization at a data server.

humanRequirements.heading: Source caveats and bounded followups
humanRequirements.text: NFS multi-domain identity mapping is not synonymous with AD forest trust. A later cross-realm variant must connect the existing Kerberos referral lesson to an explicit remote principal mapping and local permission decision; it must not assume numeric UID compatibility across administrative domains.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Implementation contract

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Use local-call/local-check/local-create events for Winlogon, LSA, SAM, token and AppInfo operations. Do not turn local OS API calls into network packets or describe every such operation as RFC protocol traffic.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Separate credential collection, validation, local logon eligibility, token creation, process creation, profile/desktop readiness, resource access and the user learning a result.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Every token has owner/logon-context/primary-or-impersonation type, user SID, attributed group SIDs, privileges plus enabled flags, integrity/elevation metadata and lifecycle; token copies are not independent authenticated users.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Keep raw input, account verifier, cached verifier, certificate/private-key handle, Kerberos credential and token as different artifacts. Permission to inspect is not possession.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Group/PAC information is attributable to its authority; local policy/alias additions are separate. Do not imply every unlock/elevation refreshes all existing tokens.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Author source/protection/decoded-acceptance events and cleanup/release histories for every readable result. Never give an observer future server/DC knowledge at request or wire receipt.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Diagram logical LSA/authentication-package/SAM/token roles within the same workstation with parent grouping. Keep no more than five horizontal actors; group or split a detailed stage.

humanRequirements.heading: Usability and teaching boundaries
humanRequirements.text: At all times show: device membership, console account authority, local process SID/account, outbound identity, effective logon/elevation policy, and current authentication-versus-authorization decision.

humanRequirements.heading: Usability and teaching boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Offer explicit local/domain and classic/Administrator-protection profile selectors before playback, with a textual explanation of what changes. Profile choice resets history rather than mutating a running principal.

humanRequirements.heading: Usability and teaching boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Provide token comparison tables and simple labels: credential verified, console allowed, token created, desktop ready, resource allowed. Separate consent, credential verification, local PIN entry and network authentication.

humanRequirements.heading: Usability and teaching boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Cross-link exact accepted SMB/AD scenario IDs and retain return-to-origin context; avoid duplicating catalog entries that merely restate an existing protocol flow.

humanRequirements.heading: WLOG01 - Workgroup workstation: local password logon
humanRequirements.text: Actors: U: user; L: Winlogon/LogonUI and credential provider; A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role; P: user process/session and kernel token role; S: local SAM authority

humanRequirements.heading: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: Required event sequence

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: collect · local-input · U → L : Select WORKGROUPPC\bob and enter the synthetic password. Credential collection is not authentication. Boundary: No authenticated identity or token yet. Artifacts: account-scope, credential-input-buffer.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: submit · local-call · L → A : Submit the declared interactive-logon request and selected authentication package. Boundary: Local IPC, never an HTTP/NTLM challenge exchange. Artifacts: interactive-logon-request.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: verify · local-call · A → S : The local package validates the submitted credential against the SAM account authority and returns account/group data. Boundary: Only S/A learn verification success at their actual boundaries. Artifacts: local-account-verifier, validation-result.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: authorize · local-check · A → A : Evaluate console logon rights and account restrictions, then form the new logon session and primary token. Boundary: Authentication alone does not bypass an explicit deny right. Artifacts: local-logon-policy, logon-LUID, primary-token.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: desktop · local-create · A → P : Attach the token to userinit/shell startup, load the selected profile, then mark desktop ready. Boundary: Token availability precedes successful profile/desktop startup. Artifacts: primary-token, profile, desktop-session.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: access · local-check · P → P : Evaluate one declared file DACL with this token; record grant separately from sign-in. Boundary: A signed-in user can still be denied a file. Artifacts: file-security-descriptor, access-decision.

humanRequirements.heading: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: Preconditions
humanRequirements.text: WORKSTATION is an ADDS member; CORP\alice exists; DC/DNS/time and machine relationship work.

humanRequirements.heading: Preconditions
humanRequirements.text: Select AES password preauthentication; no NTLM fallback in this fixture; FAST disabled only to isolate WLOG06.

humanRequirements.heading: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: Required event sequence

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: input · local-input · U → L : Collect explicitly scoped CORP\alice input and submit to the local Kerberos authentication package. Boundary: LSASS submission is not a network request. Artifacts: credential-input, logon-request.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: as · network-exchange · A → K : Run existing AS request/reply model, including selected preauth metadata, client-derived key and KDC-owned authoritative key. Boundary: No clear password crosses the KDC leg. Artifacts: AS-REQ, AS-REP, user-account-key, KDC-user-key, opaque-TGT.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: as-accept · local-verify · A → A : Decrypt and validate the client part before acquiring the issued TGT session key and installing the opaque TGT. Boundary: Ticket receipt is distinct from usable credential acquisition. Artifacts: accepted-TGT-credential.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: host-ticket · network-exchange · A → K : Request host/workstation.corp.example for the workstation itself and validate its TGS reply. Boundary: Do not stop the sign-in explanation at receiving a TGT. Artifacts: host-TGS-REQ, host-ticket, host-session-key.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: local-ticket-check · local-call · A → M : The workstation Kerberos runtime interprets its host ticket and validated authorization data using its own service identity. Boundary: This is local workstation processing, not a fabricated network AP exchange to another host. Artifacts: host-ticket, validated-logon-information.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: token · local-create · A → P : Combine validated domain identity/group information with local policy/alias membership and logon rights; create the primary token and start the session. Boundary: Token issued locally, not sent by KDC. Artifacts: domain-SID, group-SID-set, local-policy, primary-token, desktop-session.

humanRequirements.heading: Required event sequence
humanRequirements.text: network-boundary · teaching-link · P → P : Offer a separate network-resource lesson using the retained credential context. Boundary: Desktop success does not authorize a share/file. Artifacts: credential-context-reference.

humanRequirements.heading: Linux and macOS workstation login and privilege elevation
humanRequirements.text: Linux and macOS workstation login and privilege elevation

humanRequirements.heading: Linux and macOS workstation login and privilege elevation
humanRequirements.text: 17 scenarios: LLOG01-05, LELEV01-04, MLOG01-05 and MELEV01-03. This is a worker implementation plan against the accepted corrections2/source baseline; it is not a report of executed Linux/macOS integration tests.

humanRequirements.heading: Product placement and boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Product placement and boundaries

humanRequirements.heading: Product placement and boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Use the dedicated Workstations workspace with Windows, Linux and macOS sign-in and elevation/local-authorization families. Keep LSM enforcement as a topic inside local authorization. SSH remains in its existing remote-access group, linked from relevant logon lessons; its network authentication must not be reimplemented here. SMB/NFS remain resource-access continuations.

humanRequirements.heading: Product placement and boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Use a shared explanation panel for identity lookup → authentication → admission/authorization → session or operation , but do not force all systems into an identical execution order. Always display three distinct identities when relevant: requester, authenticated identity, and execution target. Local UID/account, realm principal, directory object and IdP subject can be related without being identical.

humanRequirements.heading: Reference profiles and evidence requirements
humanRequirements.text: Reference profiles and evidence requirements

humanRequirements.heading: Reference profiles and evidence requirements
humanRequirements.text: The source snapshot date is 2026-10-21 . Source metadata below records observed publication/version information. Live pages are not immutable release pins. Before implementation sign-off, freeze each used source with resolved URL, retrieved date, title, section, revision/commit when available, and content hash. Record actual OS/build, packages, hardware, PAM stack, NSS configuration, SSSD provider, access policy and cache settings for every empirical claim.

humanRequirements.heading: Reference profiles and evidence requirements
humanRequirements.text: Linux profiles are explicit compositions, not a fictitious universal Linux distribution. The reference systemd page identifies version 262; that does not establish the version shipped by any selected distribution. Use a reproducible vendor-supported machine image for native evidence and its installed manuals/configuration. RHEL 9 offline-cache documentation is a named provider profile, not a claim that all providers share its defaults. SELinux and AppArmor require separate loaded-policy fixtures.

humanRequirements.heading: Reference profiles and evidence requirements
humanRequirements.text: Apple documentation observed here includes macOS 27 capability gates. Pin the selected OS and extension and distinguish support from deployment configuration. Keep Apple silicon/T2 FileVault behavior separate from unsupported hardware generalizations. Archived Authorization Services documentation supports conceptual rights boundaries only; it does not justify implementing deprecated privileged-execution APIs. Apple OSS main code is not automatically the source of the installed macOS binary.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Shared implementation contract

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Represent PAM auth, account, password and session calls separately. NSS obtains identities; it does not prove a password. pam_systemd registers/manages a session where configured. LSM means Linux Security Modules and enforces access policy; it is not a network logon protocol.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Use local-event rendering for PAM calls, sudo policy checks, biometric decisions, keychain operations and kernel checks. Only actual sourced network exchanges get wire-message semantics. Do not invent undocumented Apple wire formats.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Keep offline cached verifier, retained TGT, newly issued TGT, sudo timestamp, polkit temporary authorization, Apple authorization reference, secure token and bootstrap token as different object types, owners and lifetimes. No cache object silently transforms into another credential.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Each scenario has deterministic success/denial branches with phase-specific stop points. Receiving authentication success cannot bypass a later policy gate. Local sessions may survive a failed remote request; the denial must not erase unrelated pre-existing holdings.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Reuse accepted field replay and held-object contracts: registered local operation names, correct actor/read grants, visible creation/use/verification/eviction and source cursors. Keep configuration inspect-only; do not generate a replay action from descriptive policy prose.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Use existing Kerberos/AD/SSH/service models through explicit links or shared subflows. Standalone Kerberos AS/PKINIT/FAST is not duplicated here. Ordinary Linux or Mac login must not be advertised as always obtaining a TGT.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Provide a compact outcome panel: local identity, network identity, authenticated by, authorization decision, resulting session/operation, and retained credentials. In advanced view show the exact profile and reason the branch stopped.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation and verification order
humanRequirements.text: Implementation and verification order

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation and verification order
humanRequirements.text: Land the shared identity/admission/session data contract and LLOG01/MLOG01, with no platform-specific network assumptions.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation and verification order
humanRequirements.text: Add online/offline directory and explicit ticket boundaries; link existing Kerberos and resource-access lessons.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation and verification order
humanRequirements.text: Add sudo/su/polkit and Mac scoped authorization; exercise alternate authenticated/target identities and no-prompt policy branches.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation and verification order
humanRequirements.text: Add LSM, FileVault/token boundaries and managed Platform SSO methods with explicit support gates.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation and verification order
humanRequirements.text: Run focused model/held-object/replay tests and mounted usability checks. Native integration evidence should use isolated test machines, synthetic accounts and read-only observation where possible, with OS/package/config hashes. Missing platform access must be recorded as unverified, never converted into synthetic pass logs.

humanRequirements.heading: Implementation and verification order
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance evidence must include identity lookup success with authentication failure; authentication success with admission denial; offline success without a new TGT; policy denial despite cached authentication; non-root execution targets; root/no-password configuration; LSM denial after elevation; FileVault eligibility independent of administrator membership; and canceled/unsupported biometric approval. A network-only IdP administrator must fail secure-token/ownership-only operations.

humanRequirements.text: Shared implementation and review requirements

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Create a dedicated Kubernetes navigation/workspace group with Human access, Token validation, Authorization/RBAC, Workload identity, and Delegation/extensions families. JWT foundations are their own shared family linked from K8s and existing OAuth/OIDC/JWE lessons. Do not bury Kubernetes inside generic OAuth or silently duplicate existing lessons.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Use canonical events, explicit actor-local holdings and immutable artifact/generation IDs. Track received bytes, parsed untrusted claims, verified signature, validated claims, mapped userInfo, authorization input/verdict, admission proposal/verdict, persisted object and response separately. Reading a claim never creates permission.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Model API authentication/RBAC/admission as local API-server stages; different swimlanes may explain responsibilities but must not fabricate network hops. The API server may read from watch caches; a symbolic storage boundary must not imply every read makes a new etcd network RPC.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Each scenario has a fixed happy path and independently selectable failures with declared policy. Branches must alter the relevant request/claim/key/rule/state, not only the narration. Do not silently recover into another authenticator or grant.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: JWT validation requires primary-source rules and profile-specific requirements. Public key retrieval is not proof of trust by itself. Never expose issuer private keys, refresh tokens or plaintext JWE contents to actors that do not possess them. Bearer token display is synthetic and clearly labeled.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Maintain overview/field/exact-object replay parity. Exact history must retain token envelope versus decrypted/validated representation, principal origin, binding rule and namespace; backwards seek must rebuild state deterministically and clear stale grants/results.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Provide a visible decision strip: credential → identity → requested action → matching grant → admission when relevant → result. Show why a step is skipped. Error cards name failing stage, caller identity, actual status and next meaningful action; do not map all 403s to RBAC.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Navigation, source/profile expanders and scenario switches need keyboard focus return, readable 390px layout, no token overflow, accessible branch labels and no color-only success signal. Keep five or fewer actors horizontally; break browser/login and API authorization into linked phases without losing artifacts.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Source panel pins release/profile/feature maturity, RFC section or Kubernetes section, retrieval date, implementation-specific cache policy and limits. Mark symbolic fixtures as symbolic; cryptographic validity requires separately computed test vectors rather than decorative signatures.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Tests should prove state boundaries and failure behavior, not mirror prose. Test route registration, all declared scenario IDs, preservation of existing OIDC/JWT/JWE paths, policy reset, identity mapping, exact-request RBAC decisions, JWT/key/token rotation, representation custody, no post-rejection persistence, and actual mounted field-to-exact-history transitions.

humanRequirements.heading: Shared implementation and review requirements
humanRequirements.text: Before claiming runnable Kubernetes conformance, validate config/manifests and critical status/feature behavior against pinned v1.37.1 executable or source. Native-browser evidence remains separate from DOM tests and from live Kubernetes interoperability. Report any source discrepancy instead of inventing a consensus.

humanRequirements.text: verify: Finish signature verification before trusting claim values. Held state: Received/decoded claims retained as untrusted evidence.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: context: Match exact issuer and intended audience; accept aud string or array only as allowed by profile. Held state: Issuer/audience observations identify expected and actual values.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: time: Evaluate exp, nbf when present, and separately declared iat/max-age policy. Held state: Clock/skew inputs shown; iat is not itself an expiration time.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: types: Validate required strings/arrays/numbers and subject semantics; then build accepted identity. Held state: Invalid types cannot coerce into an accepted subject/group.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: Wrong issuer/audience, expired/not-yet-valid, missing required claim, milliseconds mistaken for seconds, or string exp rejected.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: Duplicate claim names are rejected by this stricter demo parser; do not claim every conforming JWT parser must choose that option.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: Boundary tests use deterministic timestamps and profile-required vs optional badges.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
humanRequirements.text: No rule says all registered JWT claims are universally required.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT07 - Issuer, audience, time and claim types
JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: Teach purpose-specific validation and the Kubernetes ID-token integration as a deliberate profile.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: Actors: OIDC client; Issuer; Ordinary resource API; Kubernetes API profile

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: OIDC client audience demo-native; ordinary API audience https://api.demo.example; RFC9068 access-token typ at+jwt; separate validators.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: issue: Issue ID token for client authentication and access token for resource access. Held state: Different exact artifacts, audiences, lifetimes and intended consumers.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: client: Client validates ID token including transaction nonce when used. Held state: Client login state is distinct from API authorization.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: resource: Ordinary API applies RFC9068 type, issuer, audience and authorization profile. Held state: ID-token substitution fails this resource profile.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: kubernetes: Link to K8S01, whose configured OIDC integration deliberately sends an appropriate ID token as bearer credential. Held state: No inference that all APIs accept ID tokens, or every access token is a JWT.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: Wrong-purpose token with a valid signature rejected using mutually exclusive profile rules.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: A typ value alone never proves purpose; compare expected audience/issuer and required claims too.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: Do not invent mandatory typ=id_token in OIDC Core or K8s.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
humanRequirements.text: Do not assert the API server universally distinguishes ID vs access tokens by their origin; show which actual configured check fails.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT08 - ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Separate token validity, proof of possession and current server-side status.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Holder; API; Introspection endpoint; Local JWT validator

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Bearer profile over TLS; opaque-token comparison uses authenticated RFC7662 introspection; no DPoP/mTLS claim.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: present: Send same valid bearer token twice within validity interval. Held state: Each request obtains received credential; jti alone creates no replay cache.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: local: Local validator checks JWT with cached keys and context. Held state: No automatic revocation call or issuer session check occurs per request.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: introspect: For opaque comparison, API authenticates to introspection and evaluates active plus intended resource/profile. Held state: Introspection result has explicit cache TTL and evaluation time.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: expire: Advance clock or change introspection status; show differing rejection points. Held state: Rejected requests produce no new authorization grant; prior completed actions are not undone.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Do not present signing or JWE encryption as sender binding.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Introspection timeout follows declared fail-closed policy; cached results remain bounded by declared policy.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Logout does not imply immediate invalidation of every self-contained JWT.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
humanRequirements.text: Link existing sender-constrained flows if available instead of duplicating them; distinguish OAuth bearer errors from K8s Status responses.

humanRequirements.heading: JWT09 - Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: Show the complete client login, token authentication and authorized Kubernetes read.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Alice; kubectl/client-go; Exec plugin + browser; OIDC issuer; API server; RBAC; Storage

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: Pinned cluster fixture; exec credential API client.authentication.k8s.io/v1; public native OIDC client kubernetes-demo; authorization code + S256 PKCE; Alice sub alice and group readers.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: login: kubectl calls exec plugin; plugin opens system browser at issuer and validates returned state; redeems code with verifier; validates ID token/nonce. Held state: Plugin owns PKCE verifier/state/nonce; issuer credentials stay at issuer; refresh token remains plugin-local.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: credential: Plugin returns ExecCredential status.token and expirationTimestamp. Held state: kubectl obtains ID token only; API server never receives refresh token, code or PKCE verifier.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: authenticate: kubectl sends Authorization: Bearer ID-token over TLS; API validates configured issuer/key/audience/expiry and maps identity. Held state: API request userInfo appears only after validation; no browser redirect originates at API server.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: authorize: GET /api/v1/namespaces/demo-dev/pods becomes list/core/pods/demo-dev; reader binding permits Alice. Held state: Local RBAC decision records matched subject, binding and rule.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: respond: Read storage through API server and return PodList; mark admission not applicable to reads. Held state: Result bytes reach kubectl; token validity has not granted blanket access.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: Wrong PKCE verifier/state/nonce stops client login.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: No matching reader binding yields 403 after successful authentication.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: A cache-hit second request has no interactive login or per-request issuer introspection.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
humanRequirements.text: No API-server password form, automatic browser launch, or implicit Kubernetes User object creation.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S01 - Human OIDC login to kubectl API read

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Make username and group mapping inspectable before access decisions.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Actors: OIDC issuer; API JWT authenticator; Alice/Bob; SelfSubjectReview

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Structured AuthenticationConfiguration v1; username claim sub with prefix oidc:; groups claim groups with prefix team:; required tenant demo; reject mapped system: names.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: validate: Accept issuer/audience/cryptographic and configured tenant claims. Held state: Validated token is distinct from its mapped Kubernetes identity.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: map: Map alice to oidc:alice and readers to team:readers; add normal authenticated group. Held state: API builds userInfo; no role or RoleBinding is created from a group claim.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: inspect: Run kubectl auth whoami / SelfSubjectReview. Held state: Response identifies caller mapping; no persisted User or review object.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: contrast: Map Bob with observers and attempt same pod read. Held state: Bob authenticates but lacks reader binding; authorization is still separate.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Missing/wrong-type required mapping claim or failed CEL validation fails authentication.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Unprefixed group/string mismatch gives no binding match; prefix collisions must not confer system identity.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Mapping table shows raw claim, configuration, mapped value and provenance.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Email variant must check email_verified; do not use mutable email as the default fixture key.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S02 - JWT claims to Kubernetes userInfo
humanRequirements.text: Sources: Kubernetes Authenticating: user-requested OIDC source (OIDC tokens; structured configuration; client-go credential plugins; anonymous requests); Kubernetes kube-apiserver configuration v1 (AuthenticationConfiguration; JWTAuthenticator; Issuer; ClaimMappings; UserValidationRule); kubectl auth whoami (SelfSubjectReview); Kubernetes RBAC Good Practices (Least privilege; escalation risks; user identity reuse)

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Keep failed credential validation outside RBAC and admission.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Actors: kubectl; API JWT authenticator; Issuer metadata/JWKS cache

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: OIDC ID-token profile audience kubernetes-demo; RS256 fixtures; unknown-key refresh semantics labeled as implementation-specific; link JWT04-JWT07.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: receive: Receive a bearer token for a pod request. Held state: Token bytes initially untrusted; no request userInfo.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: verify: Evaluate configured issuer discovery, key/signature, audience, expiry and claim/user validation. Held state: Record first rejecting check without exposing token secrets in logs.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: rotate: Use old/new issuer keys to exercise cache hit and unknown-kid refresh. Held state: No accepted identity until key resolution and verification succeed.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: reject: Return Kubernetes 401 Status for an invalid presented bearer credential in this isolated authenticator fixture. Held state: No RBAC decision, admission decision or storage write follows.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Bad signature, expired token, wrong audience, issuer mismatch and unknown key each get their own branch.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Discovery/JWKS outage is not proof of token invalidity; label infrastructure vs validation failure while denying unauthenticated access.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: No silent conversion of invalid bearer to anonymous.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Do not invent AuthenticationConfiguration algorithm-list fields or combine --authentication-config with --oidc-*; optional flag-only comparison explicitly sets --oidc-signing-algs=RS256.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S03 - Kubernetes JWT rejection and key rotation
humanRequirements.text: Sources: Kubernetes Authenticating: user-requested OIDC source (OIDC tokens; structured configuration; client-go credential plugins; anonymous requests); Kubernetes kube-apiserver configuration v1 (AuthenticationConfiguration; JWTAuthenticator; Issuer; ClaimMappings; UserValidationRule); OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0, errata set 2 (3; 4.3; 7); RFC 8725 / BCP 225 (2; 3.1-3.12)

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Make one concrete namespaced permission decision fully traceable.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Alice; Bob; API server; RBAC rule store

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: demo-dev Role reader: core pods get/list/watch; RoleBinding read-pods subjects Group team:readers; Alice member, Bob not.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: authenticate: Accept either user token and show exact userInfo. Held state: Valid identities persist only for the corresponding request.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: attributes: Extract list/core/pods/namespace demo-dev from the request. Held state: Request attributes are explicit immutable input to authorization.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: match: Resolve binding subjects then roleRef then rule. Held state: Alice has matching path; Bob has none in the base demo chain (Node has no opinion for these non-node callers).

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: result: Return PodList for Alice or 403 Forbidden for Bob. Held state: Bob remains authenticated; no login retry, admission or protected data result.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Change namespace to demo-prod or verb to delete: Alice denied.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: A groups value named reader without an exact binding grants nothing.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Inspector displays subject → binding → role → matching rule → verdict.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Permission denial never alters or invents the JWT group claims.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S04 - RoleBinding explains Alice allowed and Bob forbidden
humanRequirements.text: Sources: Kubernetes Using RBAC Authorization (Roles/bindings; subjects; resource names; additive permissions; bind/escalate prevention); Kubernetes Authorization (Request attributes; verdicts; authorizer chain; access reviews)

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: Explain reusable rules versus the scope at which a binding grants them.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Alice; Bob; API server; RBAC

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: Independent resettable variants; custom demo-pod-reader ClusterRole; no built-in cluster-admin.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: namespace: Bind demo-pod-reader with a RoleBinding in demo-dev for Bob. Held state: Bob gains pod-read scope only in that namespace.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: compare: Request demo-prod pods and cluster nodes. Held state: Namespaced binding does not grant these requests.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: cluster: Separate fixture uses ClusterRoleBinding to grant same pod rules across namespaces. Held state: Both namespaces match; node access still absent because resource rule is pods.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: node: Separate demo-node-reader ClusterRole permits only get of named demo-node via ClusterRoleBinding. Held state: Cluster-scoped resource has no namespace attribute.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: ClusterRole existence without any binding grants nothing.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: RoleBinding roleRef Role from another namespace is not a valid cross-namespace grant; roleRef mutation is not a shortcut.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: Four object kinds have a visible scope comparison; bindings contain subjects, roles contain rules.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope
humanRequirements.text: Each variant resets policy state, so grants from previous variants cannot contaminate results.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S05 - Role and ClusterRole binding scope

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Explain how an HTTP request becomes a policy question.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Actors: kubectl; API request parser; Authorization reviewer; RBAC

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: reader role; optional isolated get pods/log grant; named configmap demo-config rule; no wildcard resources.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: parse: Compare collection GET, named GET and GET pods/demo-pod/log. Held state: Derive list vs get, core group, namespace, name and log subresource.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: match: Evaluate pods separately from pods/log; evaluate resourceNames only for the named get fixture. Held state: Evidence records all compared fields; do not infer pod log rights from pod read.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: review: kubectl auth can-i creates SelfSubjectAccessReview for exact attributes. Held state: Review result is advisory at that evaluation time, not a reusable grant or admission success.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: execute: Issue actual request and evaluate current policy again. Held state: Reads skip admission; successful response requires current authorization.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Adding a namespace flag cannot turn a cluster-scoped resource into namespaced scope.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Do not present resourceNames as a filter on an unrestricted list; a list/watch variant needs the appropriate name field selector and checked semantics.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Explain core apiGroup as empty string, and distinguish API verbs from HTTP methods.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i
humanRequirements.text: Show non-resource path example separately with lower-case HTTP verb; do not manufacture resource fields.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S06 - Request attributes, subresources and can-i

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: Prevent deny-rule and automatic-role misconceptions.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Bob; API server; RBAC bindings

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: Two custom bindings: readers gives pod reads; log-readers gives pod log get; separate group claims fixture.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: identify: Validate Bob group membership in both configured groups. Held state: Identity is accepted independently of permission computation.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: union: Gather matching RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding grants applicable to request scope. Held state: Display contributing rules; there is no RBAC deny rule overriding another grant.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: allow: Allow a request when at least one applicable matching rule grants it. Held state: Store matched-grant explanation, not a guessed generic role label.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: deny: For secrets get, no rule matches; all demo authorizers have no opinion and overall request is denied. Held state: Return 403; retain no secret data.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: Removing one grant does not remove access still granted by another binding.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: A nonmatching restrictive-looking role does not subtract permissions; a JWT group alone grants none.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: Keep RBAC additive union distinct from sequential multi-authorizer chain semantics in K8S16.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union
humanRequirements.text: system:authenticated is membership, not automatic admin permission.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S07 - Additive RBAC and group binding union

humanRequirements.text: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Show authorization success that still fails admission, and the path to storage when admitted.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Alice writer fixture; API server; Mutating admission; Validating admission; Storage

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Separate demo-writer role allows create configmaps in demo-dev; custom validation requires label training=approved; no actual production resources.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: authorize: Authenticate Alice and authorize create/core/configmaps/demo-dev. Held state: Request identity and authorization verdict exist; storage unchanged.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: mutate: Run mutating admission phase; the core fixture has no matching custom mutation. An optional annotation webhook can show mutation separately. Held state: Original proposal remains unchanged in core; an optional modified proposal gets a new representation and provenance.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: validate: Validate the proposed object against explicit label policy. Held state: Admission rejection leaves no persisted ConfigMap; rejection reason identifies admission rather than RBAC.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: persist: For accepted fixture, complete API validation and persist, then return 201 with server-assigned metadata. Held state: Stored object is distinct from request and admission proposal; read-back shows persisted bytes.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Missing label fails admission despite RBAC allow.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Invalid object schema or storage conflict has its own failure origin; do not label every non-401 as RBAC failure.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: GET/list/watch comparison bypasses admission.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence
humanRequirements.text: Use a checked API status fixture; do not hardcode one universal HTTP error code for all admission policies.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S08 - Authorized writes, admission and persistence

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Show workload credentials as Kubernetes-issued bound tokens.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Actors: ServiceAccount reader; Pod demo-reader; Kubelet; API TokenRequest issuer; Workload

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Namespace demo-dev; Pod UID pod-1; ServiceAccount UID sa-1; projected token volume; audience https://kubernetes.demo.example; requested lifetime 3600s but returned expiry authoritative.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: request: Authorized kubelet requests token for reader, audience and Pod binding. Held state: Kubelet has node credential; API signer key stays in issuer boundary; workload does not choose arbitrary identity.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: issue: API issues signed JWT with subject, issuer, audiences, lifetime and binding identifiers. Held state: TokenRequest response carries token; no automatic token Secret created.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: project: Kubelet writes projection; workload reads token file and calls API over TLS. Held state: Workload acquires token only when reading projection; file presence alone is not API acceptance.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: rotate: Kubelet requests replacement and updates projected content; app reloads token. Held state: Old/new generation and expiry remain distinct; replacement does not instantly revoke a still-valid old generation.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Cached old bytes eventually expire; file update does not magically update application memory.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: automountServiceAccountToken false prevents automatic mount, not all possible manually configured credential issuance.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Show rotation trigger as documented 80% TTL or 24h, while respecting returned expiry and selected server extension settings.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Default lesson is projected bounded token, not manually created long-lived service-account-token Secret.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S09 - Projected ServiceAccount token issuance and rotation
humanRequirements.text: Sources: Kubernetes Service Accounts (TokenRequest; permissions; authenticating service account credentials); Kubernetes Configure Service Accounts for Pods (Projection; issuer/audience flags; token rotation); Kubernetes Managing Service Accounts (Bound token lifetime; private claims; TokenReview versus offline verification)
