humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: Explain workload group membership and why token possession does not grant namespace access.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Pod reader; API ServiceAccount authenticator; RBAC

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: reader ServiceAccount in demo-dev; bound token from K8S09; no default resource permissions beyond declared cluster defaults.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: authenticate: Validate service-account token and current binding objects. Held state: Map system:serviceaccount:demo-dev:reader with groups system:serviceaccounts, system:serviceaccounts:demo-dev and system:authenticated.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: deny: Before fixture binding, request demo-dev pods. Held state: No matching grant; return 403 after successful authentication.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: bind: Resettable fixture adds RoleBinding subject kind ServiceAccount, name reader, namespace demo-dev to Role reader. Held state: Explicit grant path now matches this workload.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: group: Compare separate group binding for system:serviceaccounts:demo-dev versus global system:serviceaccounts. Held state: Highlight subject scope expansion without granting cluster-admin or wildcard resources.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: Same ServiceAccount name in demo-prod is a different principal.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: ServiceAccount namespace does not automatically restrict every permission it could be granted elsewhere.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: Distinguish singular system:serviceaccount username prefix from plural group prefix.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: No generic human OIDC group can become a ServiceAccount merely by copying a string; enforce configured human mapping boundaries.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S10 - ServiceAccount identities and RBAC subjects
humanRequirements.text: Sources: Kubernetes Service Accounts (TokenRequest; permissions; authenticating service account credentials); Kubernetes Using RBAC Authorization (Roles/bindings; subjects; resource names; additive permissions; bind/escalate prevention); Kubernetes Managing Service Accounts (Bound token lifetime; private claims; TokenReview versus offline verification)

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: Compare current bound-object checks with offline cryptographic validation.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Workload token holder; External resource service; API TokenReview; Offline validator; Cluster object store

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: External service has its own credential permitting create tokenreviews; presented token audience vault.demo.example; object-bound token not yet expired.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: submit: External service calls TokenReview using its own reviewer credential, with presented token in spec.token and expected audience in spec.audiences. Held state: Reviewer credential and reviewed token are distinct artifacts.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: review: API checks token plus ServiceAccount/Pod UID and existence; service checks authenticated and matching status.audiences. Held state: Successful review authenticates token subject; no resource permission is granted by this response.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: offline: Compare separate validator using trusted cluster discovery/JWKS, signature and issuer/audience/time. Held state: It cannot learn current Pod deletion from signed claims alone.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: delete: Delete Pod or change UID; replay token in both paths before exp. Held state: Live review rejects after documented lifecycle rules; offline path may remain valid until expiry without extra online checks.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: authenticated=true with no expected returned audience is insufficient for a custom audience.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: Pending deletion has documented 60s threshold; do not promise all deletions invalidate every validator instantly.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: TokenReview itself is not stored in etcd.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: External service performs its own authorization after authentication; local JWT validation is not an OIDC browser login.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S11 - TokenReview versus offline service-account JWT validation
humanRequirements.text: Sources: Kubernetes TokenReview v1 API (TokenReviewSpec and TokenReviewStatus audiences/authenticated/user); Kubernetes Managing Service Accounts (Bound token lifetime; private claims; TokenReview versus offline verification); Kubernetes Service Accounts (TokenRequest; permissions; authenticating service account credentials)

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Show Kubernetes issuer versus human issuer, and target-specific workload credentials.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Pod; Kubelet/API TokenRequest; Kubernetes API; External vault fixture

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Two separate projected tokens for same ServiceAccount: Kubernetes API audience and vault.demo.example; cluster issuer distinct from external human issuer.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: issue: Request each intended audience through an authorized TokenRequest path. Held state: Separate exact token artifacts with returned expiry and issuer.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: api: Present API-audience token to Kubernetes; validate ServiceAccount path and RBAC. Held state: No human OIDC claim mapping is reused.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: vault: Present vault-audience token to external service; use K8S11 review/local configured validation and external policy. Held state: Vault retains only its accepted identity/decision, not a Kubernetes RoleBinding.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: swap: Send either token to the unintended audience. Held state: Audience rejection prevents cross-service acceptance.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: TokenRequest is not unauthenticated token minting; unauthorized callers cannot choose arbitrary ServiceAccounts.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Kubernetes discovery/JWKS publishing does not make ServiceAccount issuer a full interactive OIDC login provider.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Display authentication issuer, token audience, resource endpoint and policy authority separately.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Do not claim token expiry always equals requested expirationSeconds; use returned status.expirationTimestamp.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S12 - Audience-isolated ServiceAccount TokenRequest
humanRequirements.text: Sources: Kubernetes Service Accounts (TokenRequest; permissions; authenticating service account credentials); Kubernetes Configure Service Accounts for Pods (Projection; issuer/audience flags; token rotation); Kubernetes TokenReview v1 API (TokenReviewSpec and TokenReviewStatus audiences/authenticated/user); Kubernetes Managing Service Accounts (Bound token lifetime; private claims; TokenReview versus offline verification)

humanRequirements.text: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Avoid a misleading universal status-code shortcut.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Unauthenticated client; API authenticators; Anonymous authenticator; RBAC

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Isolated variants: anonymous disabled; anonymous allowed only /livez; separately full anonymous with no pod permission.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: missing: Request pods without credentials when anonymous disabled. Held state: No identity accepted; return 401 in selected fixture.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: invalid: Present invalid bearer with anonymous enabled. Held state: Credential rejection remains 401; no fallback anonymous identity.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: anonymous: Send no credential to permitted anonymous endpoint. Held state: Map system:anonymous/system:unauthenticated; authorization still evaluates route permission.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: forbidden: In full-anonymous comparison, request pods with no matching grant. Held state: Anonymous identity exists but RBAC rejects: 403; endpoint-only mode blocks unsupported anonymous paths earlier.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Do not state all missing credentials always yield 401 or all 403 imply authenticated human.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Path allowlisting for anonymous authentication is not itself an RBAC permission grant.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Display failing stage and identity alongside response code.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403
humanRequirements.text: Use stable AuthenticationConfiguration anonymous fields; do not combine anonymous config with --anonymous-auth flag.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S13 - Missing credentials, anonymous identity and 401/403

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Explain original caller, impersonated identity and the extra authorization checks.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Demo operator; API authentication/impersonation; Target oidc:bob; RBAC; Audit

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Classic variant permits only target oidc:bob via explicit impersonate resourceNames; target gets reader through fixture. Separate constrained variant beta since 1.36 with gate state shown.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: caller: Authenticate original operator before processing Impersonate-User. Held state: Audit retains original authenticated identity; header alone grants nothing.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: check: Authorize every requested impersonation attribute; classic target restriction is identity restriction, not action/namespace confinement. Held state: Reject unauthorized user/group/extra header; no forged accepted identity.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: target: Evaluate actual pod request with permitted impersonated userInfo. Held state: Show impersonated identity and target authorization result; original permissions are not simply unioned in.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: constrain: In separate beta fixture, require identity permission plus impersonate-on:user-info:list in demo-dev, with no legacy impersonate fallback grant. Held state: Permit listed action only when all applicable checks pass; preserve original/impersonated audit provenance.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Constrained identity permission without action permission fails.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: If legacy impersonate is also granted, failed constrained check may fall back; show why that fixture is not confined.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Version/gate badge visible; no unlabelled assertion of stable constrained impersonation.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Keep scope to demo users; no node impersonation or system:masters example.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S14 - Impersonation permission and constrained variant
humanRequirements.text: Sources: Kubernetes User Impersonation (Classic impersonation; constrained impersonation beta; fallback; auditing); Kubernetes Authorization (Request attributes; verdicts; authorizer chain; access reviews); Kubernetes RBAC Good Practices (Least privilege; escalation risks; user identity reuse)

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Explain why CRUD rights on RBAC objects alone cannot delegate arbitrary power.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Limited policy editor; API RBAC REST validation; RBAC rule store

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Separate nonproduction editor can create roles/rolebindings in demo-dev; owns pod-read rights; no bind or escalate permission initially.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: role: Attempt to create role granting secrets read which editor lacks. Held state: Ordinary create authorization may pass; escalation prevention rejects; stored RBAC unchanged.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: binding: Attempt to bind a role exceeding current permissions. Held state: Bind restriction independently rejects; a new permission grant is not persisted.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: allowed: Create/bind only pod-reader rights already held at scope. Held state: After checks, persisted binding can affect later requests.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: delegate: Show separate tightly scoped bind permission for one custom role; describe escalate as separate explicit privilege. Held state: State reset and limited roleRef prevent accidental broad grants.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Having create rolebindings does not by itself permit binding cluster-admin.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Namespace editor cannot grant cluster-wide privileges via RoleBinding.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards
humanRequirements.text: Name bind/escalate checks separately from ordinary request authorization and admission.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S15 - Role creation, bind and escalate safeguards

humanRequirements.text: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: Keep three different extension interfaces distinct.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: Actors: Bearer client; API server; Token authentication webhook; Authorization webhook; Admission webhook

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: Preconditions

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: Optional clearly labeled extensions; explicit authentication.k8s.io/v1 TokenReview and authorization.k8s.io/v1 SubjectAccessReview; authenticated TLS transport; chosen cache/timeout/failure policies visible.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: authenticate: For an opaque bearer fixture, API calls token-authentication webhook with TokenReview and obtains userInfo. Held state: Remote result accepted only after transport/response validation; no access grant yet.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: authorize: Build request attributes; evaluate explicitly ordered authorizer chain and call authorization webhook if reached. Held state: SubjectAccessReview allowed/denied/no-opinion belongs to request decision, not identity validation.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: order: Compare Webhook-before-RBAC versus RBAC-before-Webhook with explicit allow/deny fixture. Held state: First decisive authorizer ends chain; all no opinion means deny; RBAC union rule is not the whole-chain rule.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: admit: For allowed write, optional AdmissionReview is a separate post-authorization interface. Held state: No TokenReview or SubjectAccessReview artifact is reused as admission approval.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: Negative cases

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: Webhook outage follows chosen failure policy/cache; do not invent one universal response.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: Earlier RBAC allow can bypass later authorization webhook; label this operational consequence.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: Acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)
humanRequirements.text: This is not the default OIDC path; no forced per-request issuer TokenReview.

humanRequirements.heading: K8S16 - Optional authentication and authorization webhooks (optional extension)

humanRequirements.heading: MCP authorization: 14 bounded teaching scenarios
humanRequirements.text: MCP authorization: 14 bounded teaching scenarios

humanRequirements.heading: MCP authorization: 14 bounded teaching scenarios
humanRequirements.text: Verified baseline, 21 October 2026: the exact user-supplied authorization tutorial is reachable. The official latest authorization link resolves to MCP 2026-07-28 . Use that dated normative specification. The tutorial explains the entry flow but its DCR-oriented registration and session-based sample must not override newer normative requirements.

humanRequirements.heading: MCP authorization: 14 bounded teaching scenarios
humanRequirements.text: Version changes the worker must implement: this revision removes the initialize handshake and protocol session IDs. Use self-contained Streamable HTTP POSTs with current request metadata, not a legacy GET/SSE/session diagram. Client registration prioritizes existing issuer-bound registration, then advertised CIMD; DCR is deprecated compatibility. OAuth 2.1 remains an Internet-Draft: MCP cites -13 while the current IETF record is -16 . CIMD similarly cites -00 while -02 is current . Preserve the dated MCP requirements, record draft versions, and require an explicit documented profile change before adopting differing later-draft behavior.

humanRequirements.heading: MCP authorization: 14 bounded teaching scenarios
humanRequirements.text: Placement: a dedicated “MCP” workspace/group with an “MCP authorization” entry, discoverable by MCP, agent, tool approval, discovery, CIMD, OAuth and upstream API. Default to MCP01; present local stdio and optional machine authorization as clearly different entry cards. Scope strings such as files:read are lab examples, not standardized MCP permissions.

humanRequirements.heading: MCP authorization: 14 bounded teaching scenarios
humanRequirements.text: Delivery scope: MCP01-MCP13 are required teaching scenarios, including proxy/security and local stdio lessons. MCP14 is an optional extension scenario. A topology or authorization mechanism being optional in real deployments does not make its required lesson optional in this worker delivery. The JSON deliveryScope field is core for MCP01-MCP13 and optional only for MCP14; scope separately describes protocol/deployment status.

humanRequirements.heading: Common implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Common implementation contract

humanRequirements.heading: Common implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Declare transport, exact MCP revision, public/confidential client type, registration method, authorization issuer, resource URI, token format/validation method and grant assumptions on every profile. Metadata discovery by OIDC endpoints does not imply an ID token or OIDC user-login grant.

humanRequirements.heading: Common implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: For current HTTP fixtures use POST /team/mcp, Accept application/json and text/event-stream, Content-Type application/json, MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28, matching body _meta protocolVersion/clientCapabilities, Mcp-Method and applicable Mcp-Name. Validate mirrored header/body values. No initialize, Mcp-Session-Id, GET/DELETE lifecycle, legacy HTTP+SSE or connection-wide authorization in default lessons.

humanRequirements.heading: Common implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: All remote authorization/server endpoints use HTTPS in the production teaching profile. An explicitly labeled loopback callback is distinct from allowing insecure production token endpoints. Do not turn tutorial development shortcuts into defaults.

humanRequirements.heading: Common implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Authorize each HTTP request to the protected MCP endpoint. Model four separate decisions: AS authentication/consent; resource token validation; operation/resource policy; host approval to invoke a tool. MCP clientInfo is descriptive metadata, not client authentication.

humanRequirements.heading: Common implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: No live OAuth discovery, credential entry, redirects, tool execution or arbitrary URL fetching in the offline product. Use fixed fixtures and simulated traffic. All endpoint/key/token strings are synthetic; export/share redaction must hold even in error paths.

humanRequirements.heading: Common implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Each diagram chapter uses at most five simultaneously expanded actors. Proxy lessons have two linked authorization chapters with persistent token/issuer/resource comparison rather than a six-party unreadable ribbon.

humanRequirements.heading: Common implementation contract
humanRequirements.text: Use reusable OAuth/PKCE/JWT machinery where semantically identical, but author MCP metadata/resource/scope behavior explicitly. Shared modules must not cause the dedicated JWT or existing Web profiles to inherit MCP-only requirements.

humanRequirements.heading: Exact objects and state boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Exact objects and state boundaries

humanRequirements.heading: Exact objects and state boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Author metadata documents and validated configuration records separately. Receipt of JSON creates untrusted possession, schema/identity validation creates usable configuration, and selection creates an issuer binding. Changing issuer cannot silently repurpose existing credentials.

humanRequirements.heading: Exact objects and state boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Maintain distinct exact objects for client registration, per-user/per-client consent, browser AS cookie, OAuth transaction/state, verifier/challenge, authorization code, access-token generations, refresh-token generations, R-local validation context, host approval and tool result. Token objects carry issuer/resource/client/grant links; an identical scope label is not a cross-resource permission.

humanRequirements.heading: Exact objects and state boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Field and exact-object replay include actual local creation, TLS recovery, parsing, verification, policy, acquisition, rejection, replacement and cleanup steps. Do not use inspect-only glossary context for operational checks or hide secret creation inside a wire payload. Keep field-only and exact histories consistent at their source cursor.

humanRequirements.heading: Exact objects and state boundaries
humanRequirements.text: TLS wire ciphertext is not application plaintext. A recovered JWT is not a verified token; an introspection response is not accepted authorization until its endpoint/context and status are checked. A server denial becomes client knowledge only after delivery/acceptance.

humanRequirements.heading: Exact objects and state boundaries
humanRequirements.text: PKCE verifier remains at C until the token request to A; no verifier at browser authorization endpoint or R. AS browser cookies remain browser/AS artifacts. Refresh tokens go only to A. Upstream tokens remain at the proxy/upstream hop and never appear in MCP tool outputs.

humanRequirements.heading: Exact objects and state boundaries
humanRequirements.text: Failed transactions end with explicit actor knowledge and usable-credential state. Preserve valid unrelated grants and historical possession; cancellation, expiry, revocation, authority invalidation and local deletion are not interchangeable.

humanRequirements.heading: Version-sensitive details that require explicit tests
humanRequirements.text: Version-sensitive details that require explicit tests

humanRequirements.heading: Version-sensitive details that require explicit tests
humanRequirements.text: Discovery: prefer the challenge pointer; otherwise path-specific then root PRM URI. For path-bearing issuers, test the exact three-endpoint OAuth/OIDC order. Validate resource and issuer separately. Never infer endpoints from the MCP server origin.

humanRequirements.heading: Version-sensitive details that require explicit tests
humanRequirements.text: Response issuer table: advertised support plus absent iss rejects; any present iss must exactly match the recorded issuer, even if support was not advertised; absent advertisement and absent iss may proceed under the remaining checks. Apply issuer validation before token redemption and before trusting error text.

humanRequirements.heading: Version-sensitive details that require explicit tests
humanRequirements.text: Check advertised PKCE support before authorization; this MCP profile refuses when code_challenge_methods_supported is absent. Use S256 and a fresh transaction/verifier. Model state as correlation/CSRF protection, not as a replacement for PKCE or issuer validation.

humanRequirements.heading: Version-sensitive details that require explicit tests
humanRequirements.text: The default OAuth 2.1 token request does not require redirect_uri: retain redirect validation at authorization/callback. A server needing the older OAuth 2.0 token-request parameter is an explicitly labeled compatibility profile, not a universal MCP requirement.

humanRequirements.heading: Version-sensitive details that require explicit tests
humanRequirements.text: Scope guidance can differ from metadata scopes_supported. Step-up unions previous requested scopes with the operation challenge and bounds retry attempts. Public-client refresh rotation is the selected MCP behavior; refresh issuance itself remains discretionary.

humanRequirements.heading: Version-sensitive details that require explicit tests
humanRequirements.text: CIMD is supported only when advertised and validated. DCR belongs to a labeled compatibility input, not the primary onboarding. Persist pre-registered/DCR credentials per exact issuer. CIMD identifier portability never implies bearer/refresh token portability.

humanRequirements.heading: Phase 0 - safe follow-up and a measured performance foundation
humanRequirements.text: Make the narrow WIN-11 repair. In src/windows-auth-lab.js , author the host-local creation of the acceptor subkey in the field-operation ledger for the raw CredSSP AP-REP path. Keep the same artifact, creator/holder, plain representation, source event and exact-value reference. The affected scope is the six fixed W09/W11/W13/W14/W15/W16 presets and their seven named variants listed in corrections2/windows-recheck.txt . Their exact held-object histories and client acceptance boundaries are already correct. Never add the plain subkey to wire objects to make it visible to field replay; never duplicate the existing held-object creation. A host-local operation before the AP-REP send, or a separately authored local preparation event, is acceptable when its projection and carrier boundaries remain consistent.

humanRequirements.heading: Phase 0 - safe follow-up and a measured performance foundation
humanRequirements.text: Verify that repair narrowly. One focused regression across the affected builder paths must show host creation → client validated installation in field replay, unchanged exact-object history, no plaintext key send/receive, and no early client possession. Include an unaffected local-preparation path as the control. Use the existing attribute/held-object replay APIs, not a new fixture-only substitute. Rebuild and check the affected emitted journey when the authoring shape changes. Do not rerun the complete legacy browser matrix or full suite solely for this minor presentation fix.

humanRequirements.heading: Phase 0 - safe follow-up and a measured performance foundation
humanRequirements.text: Measure the accepted build before selecting an optimization. Retain the accepted source/HTML as an immutable comparison input. On the same machine/browser/runtime, measure accepted → optimized foundation and, later, optimized foundation → complete expansion. Record cold readiness, human-query picker filtering, selection, replay start and search during active playback in source HTTP, standalone HTTP and standalone file: . Use equivalent queries and actual UI actions in both versions, alternate fresh contexts, retain every sample and document warm-up/cache conditions. A small sample is descriptive, not statistically conclusive.

humanRequirements.heading: Phase 0 - safe follow-up and a measured performance foundation
humanRequirements.text: Preserve the existing material threshold. A flag requires both a median increase above 25% and above 100 ms for startup, or above 25% and above 50 ms for an interaction. Preserve flagged raw observations and investigate them; do not adjust the threshold to make an optimization pass. The seven historical flags belong to predecessor artifact 92ab1782… ; a new accepted-build baseline neither remeasures nor silently clears that older comparison.

humanRequirements.heading: Phase 0 - safe follow-up and a measured performance foundation
humanRequirements.text: Optimize the measured cost, then proceed with catalog growth. Existing historical traces implicate the larger visible field index's paint/prepaint/layout work and picker/catalog layout. Reconfirm on the accepted current build with the permanent tools/verification/profile-expansion-replay.mjs approach, including the real index-open/index-closed control. Raw CPU profiles and Chrome traces are attribution evidence; do not substitute their instrumented times for uninstrumented acceptance medians or sum overlapping inclusive trace durations.

humanRequirements.heading: Phase 0 - safe follow-up and a measured performance foundation
humanRequirements.text: Concrete investigation points are AuthFlowStudio.renderAttributeIndex() , indexContext() and renderCatalog() in src/app.js , plus filterScenarioOptions() and ScenarioPicker.render() in src/scenario-picker.js . The current index sorts and constructs field rows, resolves scenario contexts and usage counts; keyed row reuse already avoids some replacement. The picker normalizes option text while filtering and rebuilds grouped results. Start with reusable sorted static metadata, pre-normalized search text, indexed membership and revision-keyed usage/context data, then measure whether DOM/paint work still dominates. These are hypotheses, not a prescribed optimization outcome.

humanRequirements.heading: Phase 0 - safe follow-up and a measured performance foundation
humanRequirements.text: Cache immutable catalog data separately from context-dependent definitions and canonical step usage. Key scenario/configuration caches by their real context/revision, normalized configuration and relevant authenticator/profile; invalidate on Apply, Reset, route/profile change and model replacement. Do not cache rendered identity/realm/issuer values across environments. Do not regenerate every model merely to display step counts. No global index rebuild belongs in the animation-frame loop. Any DOM reduction, containment, incremental rendering or windowing must preserve logical result order, selected-row identity, keyboard reachability, active-descendant validity and screen-reader availability. Do not declare success by silently closing the default field pane, removing global discovery, skipping results or changing the benchmark question. Retain the existing journey-scoped initial index for profiled lessons and global typed search.

humanRequirements.text: Existing Web sign-in, SSH access, Kerberos, Windows access, Network access Keep existing workspace IDs and family routes in src/workspaces.js . Add related-learning links where useful. Do not reclassify an accepted scenario solely to populate a new navigation group.

humanRequirements.heading: Navigation and cross-group journeys
humanRequirements.text: Workstations New routed workspace; Windows sign-in/elevation, Linux sign-in/elevation and macOS sign-in/elevation families. Each opens a curated beginner journey. Local logon identity, network credentials, session creation and privilege/authorization decisions are separate. PAM identity/authentication processing and LSM enforcement are not one actor or one acceptance result.

humanRequirements.heading: Navigation and cross-group journeys
humanRequirements.text: Files New routed workspace for the planned NFS profiles and a clearly labeled SMB shortcut. The SMB shortcut opens the existing canonical #/windows/files/… scenario. It is a navigation link, not a duplicated model, alias counted as a new scenario, or silent route migration.

humanRequirements.heading: Navigation and cross-group journeys
humanRequirements.text: Foundations Keep SPAKE2/SPAKE2+; add the JWT structure/validation family with related links from Web, Kubernetes and MCP. A token representation and a successful signature check do not themselves identify the receiving application's principal or authorize an action.

humanRequirements.heading: Navigation and cross-group journeys
humanRequirements.text: Kubernetes Dedicated workspace with authentication/identity, workload identity and API authorization/RBAC families as defined in the Kubernetes chapter. Token receipt, verifier acceptance, username/groups mapping, request attributes and role-binding authorization must remain distinct visible stages.

humanRequirements.heading: Navigation and cross-group journeys
humanRequirements.text: MCP Dedicated workspace for the researched MCP authorization profiles and failure/comparison journeys. Keep the MCP client, protected resource and authorization server roles explicit; source/profile assumptions determine their boundaries.

humanRequirements.heading: Navigation and cross-group journeys
humanRequirements.text: Use relatedLessons and the existing renderLearningProfile() related-journey controls for three explicit learning paths: (1) nonjoined local workstation sign-in → explicit domain credentials → the accepted SMB access journey; (2) local/Linux/macOS session → the selected NFS authentication/identity-mapping profile → file access decision; (3) JWT validation → Kubernetes authentication and RBAC, or the appropriate MCP protected-resource flow. Label what carries conceptually into the next lesson and what new credentials, trust or configuration it assumes. Following a link starts the destination's authored context; it must not imply that browser navigation transferred a real ticket, token, logon session or elevated privilege.

humanRequirements.heading: Navigation and cross-group journeys
humanRequirements.text: If a genuinely continuous demonstration is needed, author one composite canonical model with namespaced event/object IDs and explicit handoff events, mappings and credential lineage. Do not concatenate step arrays blindly or pass hidden mutable authentication state between independent lessons. A local account may access a domain resource using separately supplied credentials without changing its local desktop identity; the path must explain that distinction before Play. An NFS branch must use its own stated security flavor and identity-mapping assumptions rather than inheriting SMB's result. In an AUTH_SYS lesson, label UID/GID information as client-asserted; TLS channel authentication must not silently turn that assertion into cryptographically authenticated per-user identity.

humanRequirements.heading: Concrete code integration and module ownership
humanRequirements.text: Scenario modules Use src/lab-common.js primitives. Proposed modules: src/nfs-access-lab.js , src/windows-logon-lab.js , src/linux-logon-lab.js , src/macos-logon-lab.js , src/jwt-validation-lab.js , src/kubernetes-auth-lab.js , src/kubernetes-rbac-lab.js and src/mcp-auth-lab.js . Split sizeable elevation families into their own modules. Keep Windows remote access in the accepted windows-auth-lab.js ; share narrow pure authoring helpers where they represent the same semantics, not merely similar labels.

humanRequirements.heading: Concrete code integration and module ownership
humanRequirements.text: Registries and model metadata Add family-prefixed exports to src/lab-catalog.js : attributes, sources, scenarios, models and topics. Require globally unique field/model/event IDs and validate collisions before merging spread objects or constructing LAB_MODELS ; silent last-wins overwrite is unacceptable. Keep lookup/index construction outside playback. Add model profile, prerequisites, objective, support note, related lessons and source sections using the current metadata contract.

humanRequirements.heading: Concrete code integration and module ownership
humanRequirements.text: Navigation Extend STUDIO_WORKSPACES , STUDIO_FAMILIES , defaults and route allowlists in src/workspaces.js . Update app workspace rendering, src/scenario-picker.js , src/learning-presets.js where applicable and focus identities in src/focus-target.js . Register actual supported routes; workspaceOf() deliberately rejects unknown workspaces. Add Files' SMB shortcut as a link to an existing model rather than changing its workspace metadata.

humanRequirements.heading: Concrete code integration and module ownership
humanRequirements.text: Canonical state Use authored initialState / protocolEffects , src/protocol-state.js and AuthFlowStudio.scenarioSnapshot() . Give each new domain its own explicit state namespace. Authentication, local-session state, elevation, kernel access policy, request authorization and actor knowledge cannot collapse into a shared authenticated flag. No private UI-only history or counter may decide protocol outcomes.

humanRequirements.heading: Concrete code integration and module ownership
humanRequirements.text: Held-object authoring Add family-owned builders, for example src/held-object-nfs.js , held-object-workstation.js (split per OS when appropriate), held-object-jwt.js , held-object-kubernetes.js and held-object-mcp.js . Register every source module and builder explicitly in the two maps in src/held-objects.js . Dispatch uses exact source ownership, not a family display label. Retain createHeldObjectPlan , heldArtifact , heldAt , heldWire , coverage validation and the explicit failure for unsupported authoring.

humanRequirements.heading: Concrete code integration and module ownership
humanRequirements.text: Replay and exact values Feed the existing src/attribute-usage.js / attribute-trace.js and held-object-state.js projections. Add source-authored local operations for derivation, validation, policy checks, installation and disposal, including operations attached to a carrier event. No replay-specific mutation may fabricate acquisition or repair an incorrect source ledger.

humanRequirements.heading: Concrete code integration and module ownership
humanRequirements.text: Context and presentation Use src/runtime-environment.js and explicit src/scenario-context.js bindings for any new editable values. Apply is atomic and validated; rejection leaves the old context, selection and playback intact. Reset restores immutable examples. Extend scenario-owned actors, actor-art.js , layout.js , held-object-view.js and styles.css only as needed. Folding physical hosts never merges logical owners or changes whether an operation is local.

humanRequirements.heading: Concrete code integration and module ownership
humanRequirements.text: Offline build Register every module before its consumers in build.mjs . Its current concatenation gives held-* modules private wrappers while other modules share the emitted scope: prefix helpers or introduce an explicit isolated-module build treatment with focused bundle verification. Source-module imports passing do not prove the standalone parses. Keep dist/auth-flow-studio.html , exact script/style CSP hashes, embedded supplied icons and dependency-free offline application behavior.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Source, manifest and evidence contract

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Create a new versioned planning/evidence area, for example docs/next-expansion/ and docs/verification/next-expansion/ . Preserve predecessor reports without relabeling them. Before implementing each family, write and retain an independently authored scenario worksheet and source matrix; generate completion reports from that contract and actual results, not the product's own final-state builder. Derive the runtime inventory from this plan’s 81-core/4-optional manifest; distinguish named variants from picker choices and count the Files SMB shortcut only once. Discover actual test totals from the suite rather than inventing a target count.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Scenario row: stable ID, workspace/family, learning question, implementation/platform/version, feature/configuration prerequisites, selected protocol/security profile, normative versus deployment-specific status, actor and trust boundaries, starting holdings, source section IDs, positive/negative outcome predicates, replay focus fields, related journeys and evidence IDs. A platform support claim needs its own dated official support source; existence in a standard does not prove a shipped OS/server supports it.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Source row: primary document URL, exact section and revision/version, retrieval date, applicable errata/update relationship, supported claim and any unresolved ambiguity. Pin MCP revision, Kubernetes release/configuration and OS/client/server profile assumptions in the corresponding lesson. Mark a standards-only or uncertain profile explicitly; never convert uncertainty into an invented universal behavior. Retain small relevant snapshots/fixture inputs with hashes where appropriate and give regeneration instructions.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Message and operation ledger: sender/receiver, exact representation, protection/key/context lineage, carried versus locally computed fields, receiver-local decode/check and canonical event/milestone. Distinguish network transfer, local IPC, local computation and an exchange folded onto one physical card. PAM, LSASS and LSM processing must use their actual local subsystem boundaries; never invent network packets to connect local checks, and do not turn genuine local IPC between different owners into a self-operation. Merely listing a field in prose or payload cannot establish its ownership or replay.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Object/holding ledger: separate artifact, representation and holding IDs; creator, exact value/reference, logical owner/store, permitted readers, acquire/use/release/replace events, derived-from identity and retained authority state. A ciphertext receipt grants only the wire holding until the authored decrypt/check event. Visibility, decoding, trust and acceptance are distinct: a signed JWT payload is readable before signature/claim validation and must be displayed as untrusted, not falsely hidden as ciphertext. Decoding alone never installs a trusted identity. Grant readable or accepted state only at the appropriate authored event for that representation; do not confuse the two grants. A failed check does not erase prior credential disclosure, credentials already cached, or the evidence that a message was received.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Outcome ledger: independently state server acceptance, client knowledge, session creation, authorization decision, protected-result receipt and result verification. For denials, say who knows what and when. A JWT signature, PAM authentication result, UAC/sudo authorization step, Kubernetes role match or NFS credential mapping must not automatically imply every later access decision.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Replay invariants: full journey, connection, field and exact-object replay must reconstruct the same complete canonical prefix at the same cursor. At least one meaningful local operation and one protected receipt/acceptance boundary per family need actual mounted replay checks. Verify exact value and representation, not merely a label or number of trace rows. Check reset, seek backward, replay exit and scenario/context change for stale secrets, holdings or selected objects.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: Evidence identity: record exact source/manifest/worksheet hashes, runner hash, argv, exit status, runtime/browser/dependency versions, standalone hash/bytes, before/after identity, raw logs, screenshot hashes and findings. Keep failed/superseded runs with their status. Missing tools or incomplete scope produce an explicit unverified/partial result, never synthetic success. Reuse unchanged historical evidence only under its own identity and clearly bounded claim.

humanRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
humanRequirements.text: For numeric cryptographic claims, extend the isolated tools/verification/expansion-crypto/ verifier or a similarly isolated next-phase QA package. Pin dependencies and runtime, retain official vectors or independently generated deterministic fixtures and their provenance, and compare with an oracle independent of the application builder. Negative cases need documented mutated input and expected rejection, including wrong context/recipient/key where the profile requires it. Printing a fixture, recomputing an expected value with the same helper or passing a UI assertion is not numerical verification. Keep SYM(...) / HANDLE(...) material explicit whenever the lesson does not model real encoded bytes. No QA package becomes a runtime app dependency, no CDN/import/browser download is added to the application, and a numeric pass never becomes a live-platform interoperability claim.

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: Teaching and accessibility acceptance

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: Before Play, display the concrete question, profile/platform version, starting identities/credentials/trust and precise completion boundary through the existing learning-profile panel. Start each family with a small curated successful journey and a discoverable meaningful denial/comparison; keep advanced protocol switches out of the beginner entry flow.

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: Default to the useful physical topology; expand local actors on demand. Preserve independent PAM conversation, identity lookup, authorization/session decisions and LSM policy enforcement where the selected Linux profile models them. Explain similar Windows/macOS concepts through their own sourced subsystem roles rather than renaming them PAM. Privilege, principal, credential store and session are separate inspector facts.

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: Global search must find protocols, user questions, abbreviations, platform/profile names and relevant fields. Filtering must not activate another scenario, pause/reset playback or steal focus. Selecting a result deliberately changes context. Preserve caret/composition and platform text-editing shortcuts; maintain a valid combobox active descendant, result announcement and visible keyboard focus.

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: Keep field names and concise values readable by default; long JWTs, claims, security descriptors and key material expand in the inspector. Do not squeeze the actor graph to illegibility at narrow widths. Use the existing intentional graph-scroll/external-inventory mode and ensure sticky controls do not cover focused targets.

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: Test Tab/Shift+Tab, arrows/Home/End where applicable, Enter, Escape and F2 through workspace/family/search, graph, exact inventory, related journeys and source links. Nested help must restore the exact initiating control when it still exists. Search/index optimization must not substitute another object generation or focus a hidden legacy select.

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: Source links must have meaningful standard/section labels, be keyboard reachable, preserve safe new-tab behavior and visibly indicate external documentation. Use target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" as the current renderer does. Opening documentation is user-initiated navigation that may need connectivity; the lesson, source metadata and replay remain useful offline. Do not fetch specifications, discovery documents, JWKS or remote assets at application runtime.

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: Validate native desktop/narrow geometry, folded/expanded internals, local-operation paths, inventory overflow, long configured identifiers, reduced motion, actual touch interactions and actual browser-menu 200%/400% zoom. CSS viewport simulations are useful separate checks and must not be relabeled as real zoom. Use representative cases from every new family and dense/problematic combinations, not a screenshot of one successful default.

humanRequirements.heading: Teaching and accessibility acceptance
humanRequirements.text: G01 remains a release condition. A human must exercise the actual app with a named screen reader/browser/OS combination and record whether the scenario, current step, logical owner/holding, local versus network operation, validation result and focus return are understandable. Include search, nested help, replay/seek and at least one denial. Automated ARIA/DOM checks and screenshots do not close this gate. The worker should complete authorized implementation and produce a review candidate while an unavailable manual check is explicitly open; do not add repeated permission requests or call the candidate fully release-ready before the required manual evidence exists.

humanRequirements.text: Bounded delivery sequence

humanRequirements.heading: Bounded delivery sequence
humanRequirements.text: Delivery Scope and evidence before moving on

humanRequirements.heading: Bounded delivery sequence
humanRequirements.text: P0. Preserve and improve the foundation WIN-11 safe fix; fresh accepted-build measurements; attributable index/picker optimization; focused replay/focus/search-during-playback checks; before/after native timing and raw profiles. Freeze the optimized baseline for expansion comparison. Do not begin mass catalog addition while the measured growth bottleneck is unexplained.

humanRequirements.heading: Bounded delivery sequence
humanRequirements.text: P0-P1. Shared contract and navigation Source/profile matrices, manifests, collision checks and the new grouped navigation/routes. Integrate one representative authored lesson and holding builder per new workspace as a vertical slice before multiplying cases. Verify old links and the Files→SMB shortcut, keyboard navigation and emitted module registration. Mark partial families as partial.

humanRequirements.heading: Bounded delivery sequence
humanRequirements.text: P1-P2. File and workstation journeys Implement the committed Windows/Linux/macOS sign-in/elevation and NFS worksheet branches in bounded family slices. Reuse accepted SMB through explicit related navigation. Each slice gets its relevant source/held/replay/negative tests and targeted native coverage for changed boundaries; no automatic full historical sweep after every wording fix.

humanRequirements.heading: Bounded delivery sequence
humanRequirements.text: P3-P5. JWT, Kubernetes and MCP Complete JWT foundations first so later lessons reference a consistent verification vocabulary. Implement dedicated Kubernetes identity and authorization families, then MCP profiles, using their own sources/actors/acceptance boundaries. Add cross-group learning links and independent numeric QA where numeric claims are made. Do not wait until packaging to author failure predicates or exact-object histories.

humanRequirements.heading: Bounded delivery sequence
humanRequirements.text: P6. Integrate and finalize once On the frozen final candidate run the full source suite, universal held-object coverage and compiled smoke over every deduplicated choice. Exercise all new/changed scenario semantics in the three native loading modes, with representative legacy smoke and risk-driven additional checks for changed shared code. Complete the new-family geometry/keyboard/touch/actual-zoom matrix and final comparative performance run. Record manual G01 separately. Reopen broad checks only when a concrete later change invalidates their evidence.

humanRequirements.heading: Bounded delivery sequence
humanRequirements.text: Keep expensive browser/performance work separate from the bounded full regression generator to avoid measurement contention. Preserve the current run-regressions.mjs inventory discovery and bounded concurrency; tests should assert meaningful independently authored boundaries, not incidental wording. Add tests/<family>.test.mjs , tests/held-object-<family>.test.mjs and targeted mounted replay/navigation checks as warranted. Reuse held-objects-check.mjs , compiled-bundle-smoke.mjs and actual native runner infrastructure; extend coverage from the agreed manifest instead of copying historical numeric constants. A shared renderer, route or state-engine change may justify broader affected coverage; a local minor copy/projection fix alone does not.

humanRequirements.text: Final worker handoff checklist

humanRequirements.heading: Final worker handoff checklist
humanRequirements.text: Complete source, reproducible offline build and exact final standalone; a concise change summary and per-family manifest showing implemented, partial, unsupported and deferred items with explicit reasons. No silent omissions or invented fixed totals.

humanRequirements.heading: Final worker handoff checklist
humanRequirements.text: Versioned primary-source/profile matrix, independent protocol/ownership/outcome worksheets, precise support assumptions and known ambiguities. Default lessons follow the selected current supported profiles; legacy comparisons appear only when their authentication differences teach a requested distinction.

humanRequirements.heading: Final worker handoff checklist
humanRequirements.text: Fresh final source/test/manifest/runner/artifact identities, full-suite raw logs, all-choice compiled and held-object coverage, targeted three-mode native results, screenshot identities, actual keyboard/touch/zoom records, numeric QA evidence and current performance comparisons. Clearly separate automated/native/manual/live-interoperability evidence.

humanRequirements.heading: Final worker handoff checklist
humanRequirements.text: Retained failures and historical results; explicit open G01 and any remaining material performance flags or platform uncertainties. Address actionable regressions or carry their concrete release disposition; do not hide them inside a top-level passed:true .

humanRequirements.heading: Final worker handoff checklist
humanRequirements.text: One clearly named worker/reviewer handoff document, standalone HTML, source archive and verification archive. If captures are split into an overlay, document extraction and verify every referenced path/hash across the delivered pair. Generate package status/checksums and include them in the handoff; rebuild an extracted source package and compare it byte-for-byte with the delivered HTML.

humanRequirements.heading: Final worker handoff checklist
humanRequirements.text: This plan does not require another logo iteration, remote assets, telemetry, live endpoint calls or a broader deployment task. Preserve the existing CSP policy and supplied icons. Finish each authorized phase with concrete evidence and report the remaining phase scope; do not turn internal quality gates into repeated approval interruptions.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Final delivery and review contract

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Keep the worker handoff unambiguous. At each phase, use one phase-labelled artifact stem and identify its source and standalone hashes in one handoff document. The submitted set is the standalone application, buildable source archive and verification archive; the handoff points to exact evidence records. Include package status and SHA256SUMS in the verification archive instead of leaving them only in an external packaging directory.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Report plan ID → runtime ID → implemented profile → source sections → contract/tests → current evidence. Classify each row as implemented, partial, unsupported or optional/deferred. Preserve names and reasons; all core rows must be implemented before claiming plan completion.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Include the full new-family fixtures, source/profile ledger, exact synthetic manifests/configurations, build instructions, independent worksheets and raw verification logs. Copying narrative into a profile card is not completion of its event sequence.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Rebuild the extracted source archive and compare the emitted standalone byte-for-byte. Resolve every current evidence path/hash across the source and any documented overlay. Keep failed and predecessor evidence labeled and separate.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Provide readable results for source tests, all-choice compiled smoke, held-object coverage, current three-mode native checks, performance and any numeric vectors. State which results were actually executed. Automated, manual and live-platform results remain separate.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Preserve closed findings and all 214 baseline choices. Retain open G01, unresolved material performance issues and platform/source discrepancies explicitly; a top-level passed flag must not hide them.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Beginner-flow acceptance: the first viewport should expose the learning question, key starting identities, Play and the beginning of the useful flow. Put long source ledgers, platform caveats and cryptographic internals in accessible expandable details. Preserve their discoverability without making every new lesson start with several screens of prose.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: Scope boundary: logo redesign, live credential handling, external authentication calls, deployment and new unrelated protocol families are not part of this plan. Optional extensions are separately labeled. Research snapshots and platform validation still need to be captured by the worker where the detailed ledger says pending; the planning research is not a claim that those immutable bytes or live test machines were supplied.

humanRequirements.heading: Final delivery and review contract
humanRequirements.text: This document was checked for unique scenario IDs, core/optional counts, required scenario fields, internal links, accepted-baseline identity and existing-scenario cross-links. It contains implementation requirements and researched sources, not a report that the new features already pass tests.
